title: gen2seg: Generative Models Enable Generalizable Instance Segmentation
claim: A model trained on a narrow set of object types segments diverse unseen categories and styles, including fine details and occlusions.
layout: 3 rows of image-to-segmentation-map pairs, left-to-right, color-coded instance masks
description: A 3x4 grid of image pairs. In each pair, the input image sits on the left and the model's colored instance segmentation map sits on the right, on a black background. The inputs span many styles and subjects: a photorealistic render of dinosaurs, a Van Gogh-style still life with a basket and a bottle, a traditional ink painting of two cats, a photo of two girls petting goats, children with sheep in a barn, and a Lion King cartoon scene. Each object gets its own bright, distinct color (orange, blue, green, red, purple). The masks follow object outlines closely. They separate overlapping animals and people, and they trace fine details such as the bottle and the small fruits. The eye goes first to the saturated masks beside the varied source images.
caption: The model that generated the segmentation maps above has never seen masks of humans, animals, or anything remotely similar. We fine-tune generative models for instance segmentation using a synthetic dataset that contains only labeled masks of indoor furnishings and cars. Despite never seeing masks for many object types and image styles present in the visual world, our models are able to generalize effectively. They also learn to accurately segment fine details, occluded objects, and ambiguous boundaries.
abstract: By pretraining to synthesize coherent images from perturbed inputs, generative models inherently learn to understand object boundaries and scene compositions. How can we repurpose these generative representations for general-purpose perceptual organization? We finetune Stable Diffusion and MAE (encoder+decoder) for category-agnostic instance segmentation using our instance coloring loss exclusively on a narrow set of object types (indoor furnishings and cars). Surprisingly, our models exhibit strong zero-shot generalization, accurately segmenting objects of types and styles unseen in finetuning. This holds even for MAE, which is pretrained on unlabeled ImageNet-1K only. When evaluated on unseen object types and styles, our best-performing models closely approach the heavily supervised SAM, and outperform it when segmenting fine structures and ambiguous boundaries. In contrast, existing promptable segmentation architectures or discriminatively pretrained models fail to generalize. This suggests that generative models learn an inherent grouping mechanism that transfers across categories and domains, even without internet-scale pretraining. Please see our website for additional qualitative figures, code, and a demo.
